messages.subject: Intensity has 0 or negative values
parts:
Hi,
I ran the following dataProcess with defaults for my input file msstats.in (attached) and got the following error:

Error in dataProcess(msstats.in) : 
  Intensity has 0 or negative values. Please check these intensities and change them.

I then changed some of the parameters for dataProcess:

QuantData<-dataProcess(msstats.in, summaryMethod='linear', censoredInt='0', skylineReport=T, normalization='equalizeMedians')
CAUTION : the input dataset has incomplete rows. Missing feature intensities should be present in the dataset, and their intensities should be indicated with 'NA'. The incomplete rows are listed below.
CAUTION : some REFERENCE features have missing intensities in all the runs.

[there was much more to this error]

I emailed Scott Goulding because I saw that he had similar problems and he sent me his R code solution that he got from Meena. I tried to follow what he had done, but I got a different error:

sum(msstats.in$Intensity==0)
[1] NA
> sum(is.na(msstats.in$Intensity))
[1] 2010
> msstats.in[msstats.in$Intensity==0, "Intensity"]<-NA
Error in `[<-.data.frame`(`*tmp*`, msstats.in$Intensity == 0, "Intensity",  : 
  missing values are not allowed in subscripted assignments of data frames

I'm guessing there is something wrong with my input file, but I have no idea what it is.

Thank you!
Emma

messages.author: df9ba0266a9a081f
messages.subject: Re: Intensity has 0 or negative values
parts:
Thank you for sharing the data Scott.

1. MSstats expects the data should have (the number of feature times the number of MS run) rows. If not, there are incomplete rows. In your case, I found that you have separate transition list, which means multiple injection with different transition lists from one sample. So, NA for other transitions, which are not measured in certain run, should be reported in data too. (For example, Run1 has the intensity for transition1,2, but not fur transition 3,4, which will be measured in Run2. Then still NAs for transition 3,4 of Run1 are needed in the dataset) But users do not worry about it. MSstats will add incomplete rows. It need to recognize the design of experiments. 

2. I think that problem is multiple injection. As Dorota reported, MSstats currently recognized it as technical replicates and We will fix it soon.

Hope to help.

Sincerely,
- Meena
